title: Turn a loose Asimov humanoid leg over on the table, then seat its knee side plate flush in the pocket
keywords: turn a heavy part on the table
instruction: Turn the leg over on the table until the knee's bearing faces up, then fit the knee side plate: seat it flat in its pocket on the knee housing with its boss in the thigh's bearing and all nine holes over their inserts, leave the leg on its back, and move both hands clear.
context: Menlo's Asimov 1 is an open-source humanoid built from published parts (CERN-OHL-S-2.0). Left Leg Step 8 says to turn the leg so the thigh actuator's bearing faces up, then to fit the knee's outer side plate 600_08A on housing 600_10C so its protrusion enters the bearing and its holes meet the inserts. Here the leg, off the body, lies loose on its side, plate side away. At 3.03 kg it is twice the arm's 1.5 kg payload, so it is tipped toward the robot over its lower edge onto its back, not lifted; its knee bends freely against the knee actuator's own friction. Then three close fits meet on one axis: a 5 mm plate in a 5 mm pocket (0.3 mm a side), a 34.8 mm pad in a 35.0 mm bore, an 11.85 mm boss in a 12.0 mm bearing. The fingers can't follow the plate into the pocket, so it is let go just above and pressed home; tilted, it cocks. On its back the leg rests on three points: pressed over the boss it stays put, pressed near the plate's edge it rocks. The nine M3 bolts are left out.
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of the table. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. All parts are from Menlo's Asimov 1 repository (github.com/menloresearch/asimov-1, CERN-OHL-S-2.0): shapes from the maker's STEP files (the thigh from the maker's URDF mesh). Leg, as after the guide's instruction 3, off the body and loose on the table, nothing holding it: the thigh assembly (URDF left_hip_yaw_link: 1.949 kg, with its centre of mass and inertia) slotted into the knee housing 600_10C (MJF PA12, 1,069.5 cm3 at 1.01 g/cm3: 1.080 kg; the URDF's 2.48 kg knee link includes the calf's later parts), 3.03 kg in all and 54 cm long. Its knee joint is free: the housing turns on the thigh about the bearing's axis, from straight to 1.50 rad bent (URDF), against the unpowered knee actuator's published friction, 0.70 N m to start it and 0.02 N m once it moves, with 0.034 kg m2 reflected inertia (Menlo's actuator table, EC-A4315-P2-36, docs.menlo.ai/asimov/1/reference/joint-design-and-actuation). It starts straight, lying on its side along y with the shank toward -y, the housing's outer face (the plate side) upright and facing away from the robot (+x), the pocket's centre at (46, -7), 6.3 cm up. On its back, the task's turned pose, it rests on three points with that face up, about 4 degrees off level, the pocket's centre at about (31, -6), 10.3 cm up: from its side it tips 86 degrees toward the robot over its lower edge, its centre of mass rising from 6.2 to 7.9 cm (over the edge at 38 degrees) and falling to 5.3. In the outer face, the pocket for the plate: 5.0 mm deep, the plate's own outline with 0.3 mm clearance (80.0 mm across its round end, 40.0 mm across its neck, its narrow end toward the shank), with a 35.0 mm bore at its centre and nine M3 threaded inserts. Its walls stand full depth round the round end and the neck's root and fall away along the neck, where the housing's surface curves down. The thigh's flanged bearing 600_11X (12.0 mm bore, 5.0 mm wide) is on the pocket's axis, its face 11 mm below the housing's face. Plate 600_08A: aluminium 7075, a 5.0 mm sheet 149.4 mm long, 79.4 mm across its round end and 39.4 mm across its neck, 1 mm chamfers on its edges; on one face a 34.8 mm pad (5 mm), a 15 mm step (1 mm) and an 11.85 mm boss (5 mm, 0.9 mm tip chamfer); nine 3.2 mm countersunk holes; 120 g (42.6 cm3 at 2.81 g/cm3). It starts boss down in the socket (36 mm across, 12 mm deep) of an acetal kitting post 50 mm across and 30 mm tall at (20, -17), its sheet on the post's rim, its narrow end toward -y. Friction 0.3 (PA12 and aluminium on the table, on acetal and on each other). The plate rests on a holder on the bench (the post). Both arms start at their ready pose. Low-cost stand-in for a real trial (the README gives the steps): print the thigh and the knee housing 600_10C from the published STEP files and ballast them with steel shot to 3.03 kg, the centre of mass where the URDF puts it (check: tipped over its lower edge, it passes its balance point at about 38 degrees). Hinge them on a 12 mm steel pin in the flanged bearing 600_11X (or any 12 mm bearing), with a friction screw set so that a spring scale at 0.30 m reads 2.3 N to start it (0.70 N m). Cut the plate from 5 mm aluminium sheet to the STEP outline with a turned pad and boss, or print it; bring the pocket, bore, pad and boss to the STEP sizes and check them with gauge pins (0.3, 0.1 and 0.075 mm a side). Plate holder: a printed block with the 36 mm, 12 mm deep socket.
scoring: Measured at the end with an inclinometer and a ruler on the housing's face, a depth gauge on the plate's top against the face at ten points round its outline (round end, fillets, neck, narrow end), a 2.4 mm pin gauge and a tape. Score 0 if the plate or the leg falls off the table. Rungs are cumulative: 0.25 with the leg on its back on the table (the face within 10 degrees of level, at its resting height within 12 mm: lying there, not held up); 0.5 with that and the plate in the pocket's mouth, its boss's axis within 1.5 mm of the bearing's and no point of its top more than 4.0 mm above the face (the rim, pad and boss each at least 1 mm in); 0.75 with the plate seated flat, every point within 0.5 mm of flush and level with the face (tilt under 1 degree, boss down); 1.0 with that, the pin gauge passing through each of the nine 3.2 mm holes into its insert's thread (axis within 0.45 mm: 0.4 through the hole, 0.05 into the 2.5 mm minor diameter), no gripper within 10 cm of the plate and the face round it or within 8 cm of the leg's centre line (thigh's end, knee, calf's end), and the plate and leg still (plate under 1 mm in 1 s; leg under 2 mm/s and 0.6 deg/s), held for 1 s and still true at the end. A plate set in the pocket before the leg was on its back, pressed home with the leg moved 15 mm, or its face turned 3 degrees, from how it lay when the plate first reached the mouth, or never carried by a gripper (10 steps in a row 1 cm up with a fingertip within 3 cm), scores at most 0.5. No hold is needed during the press: the leg stays put on its own, so no hand should hold it. Real trial: the same gauges, tape marks round the leg, and a photo.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz. Plate, pocket and bearing are the maker's STEP geometry; no collider widened: rim 0.30 to 0.34 mm a side, pad 0.10 to 0.12, boss 0.075 to 0.09. Friction 0.3. Knee friction (0.70 start, 0.02 moving N m, 0.034 kg m2) is a coded drive; the arm presses with about 10 N. Real trial: a leg printed from the STEP files, ballasted to 3.03 kg and its centre, with a friction-set hinge; fits kept to STEP sizes (see setup).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the leg was never touched); demo: 1.0
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials, lift the plate out of the pocket with a suction cup on its top (or by its neck's flats) and set it boss down in the kitting post's socket, straighten the knee, and tip the leg back onto its side, plate side away, on its tape marks.
